builder_plan.scenario: You already need task-specific training and want to reduce its memory or compute cost.
builder_plan.change: Change only the training technique on a small controlled run after checking prerequisites.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current training recipe with the same model, data split, and evaluation.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Held-out quality, peak memory, training time, and full compute cost to the target quality.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: CertiSum: Bitwise-Identical MXFP4 Training Across Platforms and Parallelism Layouts
summary: CertiSum replaces non-deterministic MXFP4 training with a certification mechanism that ensures bitwise-identical results across platforms by verifying exactness or recomputing outputs. It costs an 11.8-60.5% increase in training-step latency relative to standard MXFP4 and requires specific hardware support for MXFP4. Failure can occur if certification rates are low, forcing expensive exact recomputation that negates performance benefits.
rationale: The reader lacks the infrastructure for foundation-model training and the specific hardware required for MXFP4, making this technique irrelevant to their production constraints.

claims.statement: CertiSum replaces non-deterministic MXFP4 training with a certification mechanism that ensures bitwise-identical results across platforms by verifying exactness or recomputing outputs. It costs an 11.8-60.5% increase in training-step latency relative to standard MXFP4 and requires specific hardware support for MXFP4. Failure can occur if certification rates are low, forcing expensive exact recomputation that negates performance benefits.
CertiSum achieves up to 1.24x speedup over BF16 and 1.70x over deterministic BF16 in MXFP4 training.
